request.description:
Everything the push dialog needs.

`tax_by_branch` precomputes CSGST vs IGST for every branch against this PO's ship-to state — the branch is the from-state for place of supply, so picking the wrong one produces a valid document with the wrong tax.

`addresses` is read live from B1 (BP addresses are not mirrored locally: one customer here has 142). If SAP is unreachable, `address_lookup_error` is set and the rest still works.

Builds the exact JSON that would be POSTed to /b1s/v2/Orders without sending it. Check VatGroup on the lines — CSGST@5 means the branch and ship-to are in the same state, IGST@5 means they are not.

422 with a readable message if the warehouse does not belong to the branch, the branch is disabled, or a line has no B1 item code.

request.description:
Invoice for the SAP-ready Blinkit PO (see Webhooks folder). Storing it raises the 856 and queues it for Blinkit in that partner's own wire format.

`batch_number` and `expiry_date` per line are what make the ASN valid — Blinkit marks both mandatory (§12.3, §12.16). Without them the ASN is still built and sent, but with warnings.

**Always read `results[]`, not just the counters.** An invoice can be stored yet HELD, with `asn_dispatched: false` and the reason in `issues[]`.

Idempotent on `invoice_number`: re-pushing updates (typically to add the IRN once the IRP responds) rather than duplicating.

Inspect the generated ASN payload afterwards on the PO detail page → Outbound tab, or via GET /api/pos/{{poId}}.

Single endpoint for add and update. Safe to send repeatedly.

HOW WE DECIDE IT IS THE SAME INVOICE
`b1_invoice_doc_entry` is tried first — it is your immutable key, so a re-push carrying it lands on the same row whatever else changed. Sending it on every push is recommended.

`invoice_number` is the fallback and stays unique. It matters because the first push of an invoice usually has no DocEntry yet (B1 assigns it on posting, the IRN later still), and the number is what the retailer reconciles against.

REFUSED, NOT APPLIED: a DocEntry we already hold arriving under a DIFFERENT invoice_number. B1 does not renumber a posted invoice, so that means a cancel-and-repost or a wrong DocEntry — and renaming a stored invoice would break the ASN the retailer already holds against the old number.

The common re-push is the IRN: push the invoice immediately (we store it and send the ASN), then push again once the IRP returns the IRN and we fill it in.

{{poNumber}} and {{buyerSku}} come from 'List POs' / 'Get PO detail'. Run those first, or hardcode real values.

ALWAYS read results[] — an invoice can be stored but HELD (asn_dispatched=false) with the reason in issues[].

batch_number takes a string here; see 'line split across two batches' for the multi-batch form.

exec: console.log('created=' + b.created + ' updated=' + b.updated + ' skipped=' + b.skipped);

item.name: Push invoice — line split across two batches

request.description:
A line filled from more than one batch. The retailer books stock against a batch and matches it at goods-in, so they need the split, not the total.

RULES
• Batch quantities must total the line's qty (34 + 16 = 50). Anything else is rejected: summing to less under-declares the shipment, summing to more declares stock that was never invoiced.
• batchNumber / batch_number and expiryDate / expiry_date are both accepted. A batch with no expiry inherits the line's expiry_date.
• The plain string form still works and means one batch for the whole quantity, so nothing already sending it has to change.

WHAT THE PARTNER RECEIVES
Two rows, not one nested field — Blinkit §12.3 types batch_number as a single string per item and Zepto's batchDetails is one object per itemDetails entry. The rows share every per-unit figure (unit_price, MRP, landing price) and divide only the quantity.

Needs a real Sales Order, like the request above: set b1_sales_order_doc_entry, or run 'List POs' first so {{poNumber}} is filled. Without one you get outcome=ERROR with 'No Sales Order found'.

exec: console.log('outcome', r.outcome, '| asn', r.asn_number, '| dispatched', r.asn_dispatched);

Held invoice (no ASN) → raises and queues it as an explicit operator override (audit-logged, held issues resolved).

Returns 409 if the ASN was already delivered and acknowledged.

Cancels the ASN at the partner and marks it cancelled here — in that order. Marking it cancelled locally while the retailer still holds it is the failure this avoids: their warehouse is the one expecting the truck.

ZEPTO   DELETE /api/v1/external/asn?asnNumber=… (contract v12 §2.b)
BLINKIT no cancellation endpoint exists — refused with that reason, since pretending otherwise is worse than saying no.

There is no update API on either side, so correcting a sent ASN means cancel, then re-invoice under a NEW invoice number. Re-using the number is rejected as a duplicate.

request.description:
Single endpoint for both. Existence is decided on `code` (= SAP `CardCode`).

• 201 — created
• 200 — updated
• 409 — the customer is soft-deleted here; restore it first
• 422 — `source_channel` is not one of API / WEBHOOK / EMAIL / PORTAL / MANUAL

WHAT AN UPDATE WILL NOT OVERWRITE
`source_channel`, `gmail_label`, `webhook_secret` and `asn_sla_hours` describe how we FETCH this retailer's orders. A SAP Business Partner record has nothing to say about that, so they are written when the customer is created and thereafter only where still empty.

This matters: `source_channel` defaults to MANUAL in this schema, so sending it on a refresh is indistinguishable from omitting it. Applying that would demote a live API customer to MANUAL and stop its PO polling with no error anywhere. It is ignored unless the field is genuinely unset.

Creating the customer does not make POs flow — ingestion also needs an adapter and a parser in our code for this code. The response `warnings` say what is missing.

Enqueues an immediate poll. Zepto requests a 14-day window and dedupes on eventId, so re-running is safe — already-seen events are skipped.

Only works from a whitelisted IP; a dev machine gets HTTP 428.
MANUAL and PORTAL channel partners.

What this partner actually buys, used to fill a keyed-in line.

Their SKU mappings come first and carry what only a mapping knows — their buyer SKU, the contracted unit price, the UoM they order in. Items the master knows but this partner has never been sold follow, flagged mapped=false, because a hand-keyed order is often for something new to them.

For partners with no integration — LOTS by phone and paper, Reliance/JioMart until its scraper is built.

Stored as a raw_message exactly like a webhook body, then parsed, validated, mapped and pushed by the same pipeline. Nothing downstream can tell it from a Blinkit webhook.

WHAT YOU SEND vs WHAT IS DERIVED
Send quantity, unit price and one gst_rate per line. Taxable amounts, the CGST/SGST-vs-IGST split, line totals and header totals are computed — a hand-typed total that disagrees with its own lines by a rupee trips TotalReconciliationRule and parks the order in the exceptions queue.

The split follows place of supply, so the ship-to needs a state or a GSTIN. Without one this refuses rather than guessing: defaulting to intra-state would put CGST+SGST on an inter-state order.

b1_item_code is optional and only meaningful here — a manual partner has no catalogue for a buyer SKU to be mapped from, so naming the item directly is what makes these orders pushable at all. It is checked against the material master.

replace_existing=false refuses a PO number already entered (on hand-keyed input that is far more likely a double submission than a revision). Set it true to file a correction, which supersedes the previous version.

item.name: 17 · Webhooks (partner → us)
item.description:
Partner-to-us endpoints. Authenticated with the `api-key` header ONLY — no login, no Bearer token. A webhook is a plain HTTP POST; there is no socket or handshake.

The Blinkit request carries the complete POVMS contract payload and full field documentation — it can be handed to Blinkit's team as the integration spec.

item.name: Blinkit — push PO (passes every validation, SAP-ready)

request.description:
End-to-end test payload. Lands as **VALIDATED with zero issues**, which the other Blinkit sample does not — it is built to satisfy every rule:

- `sku_code` values are real BLINKIT mappings (→ FG00310 / FG00233 / FG00322), so E002_SKU_UNRESOLVED cannot fire.
- Quantities are whole cases (36×10, 30×8, 36×5), so E008_CASE_SIZE_MISMATCH cannot fire.
- `basic_price` sits on the contracted price, so W004_PRICE_VARIANCE stays quiet.
- `outlet_id` 12543 has a ship-to mapping → FG_MH, so W003_SHIP_TO_UNMAPPED cannot fire.
- CGST 2.5 = SGST 2.5 with IGST null (Maharashtra → Maharashtra), so the tax rules pass.
- `total_amount` equals the sum of the line totals to the paisa, so W006_TOTAL_MISMATCH cannot fire. Each line's taxable value is a multiple of 0.40, which makes 2.5% land exactly on two decimals — otherwise our per-line tax and B1's total-level tax differ by a paisa.

Change `po_number` before re-sending: the same number is de-duplicated rather than creating a second PO.

Then push it: **Purchase Orders → Push to SAP with branch + warehouse** (bpl_id 5, whs_code FG_MH). Verified live → Sales Order 3000046 / DocEntry 1771.

# Blinkit → Let's Try Foods · Purchase Order Creation

Push a PO to us. Implements Blinkit's **POVMS - Purchase Order Creation API Contracts**
(v 2026-02-10). Section numbers below (3.6.x) refer to that document.

The body on this request is a **complete, working example** — every field in the contract
is present and the figures reconcile, so it can be sent as-is to verify connectivity.

---

## Endpoint

```
POST {{baseUrl}}/api/webhooks/BLINKIT
Content-Type: application/json
api-key: <the key we share with you separately>
```

The partner code in the path must be exactly `BLINKIT`, uppercase.
A **webhook is a plain POST** — there is no socket or handshake.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Accepted. The body is the acknowledgement — read `data.po_status` |
| `401` | `api-key` header missing or does not match |
| `404` | Partner code in the URL is wrong |
| `422` | Payload shape invalid — `details[]` names the exact field |

---

## Top level

| # | Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `type` | string | **yes** | Enum: `PO_CREATION`, `PO_CANCELLATION` |
| 2 | `po_number` | string | **yes** | Must equal `details.po_number` (3.1) |
| 4 | `tenant` | string | **yes** | Enum: `BLINKIT`, `HYPERPURE` |
| 3 | `details` | object | **yes** | Full PO metadata |

> **`tenant` matters.** `HYPERPURE` is a different legal buyer with its own GSTIN, so it
> maps to a different customer account on our side. Sending the wrong value invoices the
> wrong entity.

## details

| # | Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | `po_number` | string | **yes** | Must match the top-level value |
| — | `outlet_id` | integer | **yes** | Your DC / outlet identifier |
| — | `issue_date` | string | **yes** | ISO-8601 UTC |
| 3.2 | `expiry_date` | string | no | ISO-8601 UTC |
| 3.3 | `delivery_date` | string | no | ISO-8601 UTC |
| 3.5 | `vehicle_details.license_number` | string | no | Receiving vehicle |
| 3.7 | `total_sku` | integer | **yes** | Must equal `item_data` length |
| 3.8 | `total_qty` | integer | **yes** | Must equal the sum of `units_ordered` |
| 3.9 | `total_amount` | number | **yes** | Must equal the sum of line values |
| 3.10 | `custom_attributes[]` | array | no | Free-form `{name, value}` metadata |

> We compare `total_sku`, `total_qty` and `total_amount` against the lines we parse. A
> mismatch does not reject the PO, but it is flagged for manual review before invoicing
> and will slow the order down.

## details.buyer_details (3.4)

| # | Field | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.4.1 | `name` | string | no |
| 3.4.2 | `gstin` | string | **yes** |
| 3.4.3 | `destination_address` | object | **yes** |
| 3.4.5 | `registered_address` | object | **yes** |
| 3.4.6 | `contact_details[]` | array | **yes** — `{name, phone, email}` |

Address objects carry `line1`, `line2`, `city`, `state`, `postal_code`, `country`.
`postal_code` is required (3.4.4.5); the rest are optional.

> **Send `state`.** Indian GST requires CGST+SGST for an intra-state movement and IGST
> for inter-state. We determine which by comparing your delivery state against ours.

## details.supplier_details (3.5)

`id`, `name`, `gstin`, `pan`, `shipping_address`, `registered_address` are required;
`contact_details[]` is optional.

## details.item_data[] (3.6)

| # | Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3.6.1 | `item_id` | integer | **yes** | Your internal item ID |
| 3.6.2 | `sku_code` | string | no | **Optional but strongly preferred** — see below |
| 3.6.3 | `line_number` | integer | **yes** | Zero-based is accepted |
| 3.6.4 | `units_ordered` | integer | **yes** | Must be > 0 |
| 3.6.5 | `landing_price` | number | **yes** | Incl. logistics and taxes |
| 3.6.6 | `basic_price` | number | **yes** | **Pre-tax cost price — we bill on this** |
| 3.6.7 | `tax_details` | object | no | See below |
| 3.6.8 | `name` | string | **yes** | Item name |
| 3.6.9 | `mrp` | number | **yes** | Maximum Retail Price |
| 3.6.10 | `upc` | string | **yes** | GTIN / UPC |
| 3.6.11 | `uom` | object | **yes** | `{unit, value}` — e.g. `{"unit":"g","value":57}` |
| 3.6.12 | `crates_config` | object | no | `{crates_ordered, crate_size}` |

> **`sku_code` — please always send it.** It is the field we map to our item master. It
> is optional in the contract, and when it is empty we fall back to `item_id`, but that
> requires a separate mapping on our side and delays the order. Sending `sku_code`
> avoids the problem entirely.

> **`basic_price` vs `landing_price`.** We compute the taxable value from `basic_price`
> because `landing_price` already includes tax — using it would double-count.

### tax_details (3.6.7)

| # | Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.6.7.1 | `cgst_percentage` | number | Intra-state |
| 3.6.7.2 | `sgst_percentage` | number | Intra-state |
| 3.6.7.3 | `igst_percentage` | number | Inter-state — `null` when intra-state |
| 3.6.7.4 | `cess_percentage` | number | A **percentage** |
| 3.6.7.5 | `additional_cess_value` | number | A **flat amount**, not a percentage |

CGST+SGST and IGST are mutually exclusive. Send `null` for the ones that do not apply —
the example uses CGST+SGST with `igst_percentage: null`.

---

## Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "PO received",
  "timestamp": "2026-08-19T13:07:06Z",
  "data": {
    "po_status": "processing",
    "po_number": "2264110001440",
    "errors": [],
    "warnings": []
  }
}
```

`data.po_status` enum: `processing` · `accepted` · `partially_accepted` · `rejected`.

We return `processing` immediately — the PO is stored and queued. The final outcome
follows on the acknowledgement flow.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E101` | Duplicate PO number |
| `E102` | Outlet not found |
| `E103` | Supplier GST mismatch |
| `E104` | Buyer GST mismatch |
| `E105` | SKU-level error (MRP missing, qty over max) |
| `W101` | UOM mismatch — created with the default UOM |

**Retries are safe.** We de-duplicate on `po_number`, so re-sending the same PO updates
rather than duplicating it.
